## How it works

- [statement] Borrowing uses one universal operate call. Signed string `colAmount` (collateral) and `debtAmount` (debt), both in base units, select the action: positive colAmount deposits, negative withdraws, positive debtAmount borrows, negative repays; `positionId: 0` creates a new position NFT. POST /borrow/operate returns {nftId, transaction} (a base64 unsigned VersionedTransaction). POST /borrow/operate-instructions returns {nftId, instructions, addressLookupTableAddresses}, so the caller must load those lookup tables when compiling a v0 message. (high confidence) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/borrow/api.md · keywords: Jupiter perps and lend APIs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/openapi-spec/lend/borrow.yaml

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A perps trade is an on-chain request. The trader's action creates a PositionRequest account, a PDA derived from the Position account, constant seeds and a random counter, plus a PositionRequestATA token account that holds the tokens in transit. Non-TP/SL requests close as soon as they are executed or rejected. TP/SL requests stay on-chain until triggered. Each request has an `executed` flag. The CLI's types identify both limit orders and TP/SL orders by `positionRequestPubkey`. (high confidence) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/perps/position-request-account.md · keywords: Jupiter perps and lend APIs · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jup-ag/cli/main/src/clients/PerpsClient.ts
- [statement] The Borrow API does not wrap or unwrap native SOL. A deposit into a vault whose supply token is WSOL (So11111111111111111111111111111111111111112) fails with a token-program 'insufficient funds' error until the signer's WSOL account is funded. Wrap slightly more than the deposit, because the transfer rounds up by a few base units. Borrowing or withdrawing WSOL leaves wrapped SOL in the WSOL token account. (low confidence) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/borrow/api.md · keywords: Jupiter perps and lend APIs

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Every Borrow endpoint accepts a `market` parameter, `main` (default) or `ethena`. Vault and position IDs are scoped per market, so the same vaultId is a different vault in each. The ethena market is a separate deployment with its own program IDs. The Earn OpenAPI spec defines no market parameter. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/borrow/api.md · keywords: Jupiter perps and lend APIs · also: https://developers.jup.ag/docs/openapi-spec/lend/borrow.yaml, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jup-ag/jupiter-lend/main/README.md, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/openapi-spec/lend/lend.yaml
- [statement] Jupiter Lend's on-chain programs are published by Instadapp in the fluid-solana-programs repository, whose README is titled 'Jupiter Lend Solana Program'. Jupiter's lend skill calls the protocol 'powered by Fluid Protocol'. Instadapp's README says the upgrade authority is a 12-hour timelock multisig jointly controlled by Jupiter and Fluid team signers. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Instadapp/fluid-solana-programs/main/README.md · keywords: Jupiter perps and lend APIs · also: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jup-ag/agent-skills/main/skills/jupiter-lend/SKILL.md, https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/api-vs-sdk.md
- [statement] The Earn API guide's snippets do not run as pasted. The deposit, withdraw, mint and redeem examples never call .json() on the fetch response, and the positions example is missing a comma after the URL argument. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://developers.jup.ag/docs/lend/earn/api.md · keywords: Jupiter perps and lend APIs
